title: Traveller Club Accrual Rates Carried by the Air Ticket Fare Brands
content:
Two accrual rates are scheduled for each of the Air Ticket Fare Brands: the rate at which spendable points accrue, and the multiplier at which the same spend counts towards tier.

**Points earn rate.** The percentage of the base fare that accrues as traveller club points.

**Tier-qualifying multiplier.** The multiplier applied to base-fare spend when counting tier-qualifying points.

| Fare brand | Points earn rate (percent of base fare) | Tier-qualifying multiplier |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Basic Economy Lite | 0 | 0.0 |
| Economy Saver | 25 | 0.5 |
| Economy Classic | 50 | 1.0 |
| Economy Flex | 100 | 1.0 |
| Premium Economy Select | 125 | 1.25 |
| Business Saver | 150 | 1.5 |
| Business Flex | 200 | 2.0 |

## Points of judgement

**The two rates are scheduled independently.** Economy Classic and Economy Flex share a multiplier of 1.0 while their earn rates differ, 50 percent against 100 percent; so the multiplier never discloses the earn rate, nor the earn rate the multiplier.

**Where both are zero.** Basic Economy Lite alone is scheduled at 0 percent and 0.0, which is to say that spend under that brand neither accrues points nor counts towards tier.

**Hypothetical figures.** A hypothetical base fare of 1000.00 USD flown under Premium Economy Select accrues, at the scheduled 125 percent, 1250 points, and counts towards tier at the scheduled multiplier of 1.25, being 1250 tier-qualifying points. The same base fare flown under Economy Saver accrues, at 25 percent, 250 points, and counts at 0.5, being 500 tier-qualifying points — the two counts need not agree, because the schedule sets them separately.
